newsitem.title: UK: N Sea markets quiet, Brent holds strong.
newsitem.headline: N Sea markets quiet, Brent holds strong.

text.p: North Sea differentials held at current strong levels amid evidence of European refining demand although market activity was thin, traders said.
"Most North Sea and West African crudes are gone (sold) up to the third decade (of January). The demand is good in Europe," one trader said.
A Brent cargo loading January 19-21 sold on Tuesday at Feb Brent +20 cents. The same cargo moved on Monday five cents lower.
U.S. buyers were still staying away from the market despite a workable transatlantic arbitrage.

"You would think that with the arbitrage open the Americans would be there to buy but their margins are not great. There is some anticipation of cold weather and in a low stock situation that should bring out some buying," another trader commented.
The LR2 of Brent which loads on January 10 and is destined for the U.S. was heard already committed.
Only five cargoes of January Forties remained unsold and the grade was assessed around dated Brent +40 to +42 cents.
Action on the Brent CFD market was slow. Next week (Jan 13-17) moved early in the day at Feb +8 cents and later at March +63 cents.
Only one Brent, loading Jan 22-24, was turning wet on Tuesday and was heard still in the chains but was expected to be kept before the five o'clock deadline.
